images.final_prompt:
Create one landscape 16:9 concept image. Use case: illustration-story. 
The illustrated map of the NEW layout, in exactly the style of refs/style_map.png: a top-down hand-drawn
children's-book map on stained cream paper with crayon scribbles, thick dark hall walls, a pale green path
network, and each zone drawn as a small coloured illustration with its name on a white rounded label.
Follow refs/ref_plan.png for where everything is and how big (north is up):
- THE BIG FRAME fills the middle of the hall and almost half of the whole map: a huge block of yellow, red,
  blue and green posts and black netting, drawn as a dense grid, with a wing against the middle of the top wall.
  Labels inside it: "NET MAZE" (left part), "TUBE TOWN" (top, against the top wall, full of coloured tubes),
  "FOAM FOREST" (right part, punch bags), "THE TOWER" (top-right corner of the frame, tallest, a red spiral
  slide down its side), "BALL OCEAN" (bottom-right inside the frame: a blue pit, nearly empty, bridges over it).
- "HOME BASE": a yellow circle in the very centre of the frame with a red post and a child's stick-figure
  drawing counting 1 2 3; three winding lanes lead from it to gates in the west, south and east faces.
- Round the edge, small: "RECEPTION" bottom-left with the entrance doors and a red arrow in the bottom wall;
  "SNACK SHACK" on the left wall with picnic tables; "PARTY ROOMS" top-left; "STAFF ONLY" top-right as a small
  mustard-yellow corridor maze with a red "EXIT" door in the top-right corner; "TODDLER TOWN" bottom, left of
  centre; "INFLATABLES" down the right wall and into the bottom-right corner (bouncy castles, a green dinosaur).
- NO arcade, no prizes, no arcade machines anywhere. Exactly these labels, spelled exactly, each once.
Check the spelling of every label; regenerate if any is wrong or missing.

## What the level is
An abandoned 1990s indoor soft-play centre inside an enormous warehouse, the "Backrooms" kind of empty: nobody
there, dim, dusty, quiet. A co-op hide-and-seek horror level; players hide inside the play frame.

## What the new draft changes (this is what the pictures must show)
1. The hall is twice the floor and the roof is far higher: about 34 metres (the old one was 13). It must feel
   cathedral-high, the roof almost lost in the dark.
2. THE BIG FRAME, the multi-storey soft-play climbing structure of padded posts, net fences, mat decks, tubes and
   slides, is now nearly HALF of the whole hall and SIX storeys high everywhere (one storey = a deck about 2.8 m
   above the last), SEVEN in "Tube Town" and TEN in "the Tower". It is the size of a city block. Its slides are
   correspondingly long: tubes that drop six, seven and ten storeys.
3. The arcade is REMOVED. No arcade cabinets, no claw machines, no prize shelves, no neon anywhere.
4. Home Base (a yellow circle on the floor with a short red padded post in the middle) is a round court INSIDE
   the frame, open to the roof, with the frame rising on every side like an arena.
5. The ball pit ("Ball Ocean") is sunk INSIDE the frame with net bridges crossing above it. It is ALMOST EMPTY:
   a bare blue padded pit floor with only a few dozen loose plastic balls. Never draw a pit full of balls.

## Look, for every photoreal image
Photoreal concept art, wide lens, eye height unless stated. Lit only by sparse cold-white fluorescent strip
fixtures hanging far overhead, several dead, so there are pools of light and long stretches of shadow, with a
light haze. Slightly brighter and more saturated than a real derelict building: the colours must still read.
Materials exactly as in the references: blue-and-green checkerboard foam puzzle-mat floor, worn, a few tiles
missing over grey concrete; steel posts wrapped in yellow, red, blue and green vinyl padding; black knotted
safety netting stretched between the posts as fences and walls; coloured vinyl mat decks; square red panels
with a round clear bubble window; moulded plastic tube slides and open slides, glossy, each ONE solid bright
colour (red, yellow, green or blue; never striped, never black); exposed steel-deck roof with joists and ducts.
Scattered loose plastic balls on the floor. No people, no children, no animals, no entity unless the image asks
for it, no arcade machines, no neon, no watermark, no HUD, no UI. No lettering except the sign text an image
names; if a generation shows garbled lettering, regenerate it.


Reference roles: style images provide appearance only; ref_plan controls NEW layout and ref_height controls NEW scale. Do not copy obsolete layout, low height, striped slides, full ball pit, or text from reference images. Keep all essential content inside a 16:9 composition. This image is the illustrated map, not photoreal. Exactly once each: THE BIG FRAME, NET MAZE, TUBE TOWN, FOAM FOREST, THE TOWER, BALL OCEAN, HOME BASE, RECEPTION, SNACK SHACK, PARTY ROOMS, STAFF ONLY, TODDLER TOWN, INFLATABLES, EXIT. Also counting numerals 1 2 3. No other lettering. Make every label legible and correctly spelled.
CRITICAL CORRECTIONS: Include a prominent white rounded label reading exactly THE BIG FRAME once over the central frame. All fourteen listed labels must appear. Every tube must be one uniform solid colour along its entire length, never differently coloured segments. Clearly draw three winding ground lanes connecting Home Base to west, south and east gates. Six deck levels in the main frame, seven in Tube Town, ten in tower, while retaining top-down map readability.
images.weakness: All 14 required labels are present and correctly spelled; west/east winding lanes are obscured, storey counts are schematic, and some Tube Town tubes still change colour.
